first.rationale: Targeted promotional pricing is the most directly relevant response to the competitor’s aggressive entry pricing and has inherited evidence of acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMBs. Verification should confirm durability, qualification criteria, and any discount-related downstream value effects before committing; onboarding deterioration remains a meaningful competing constraint.

mid.rationale: Run a shortened-onboarding experiment. It directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and should also support recovery of activation, while the verified prior experiment showed higher completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and a 3% increase in 30-day retention. Promotional pricing is ruled out for this cycle because its verified qualified-revenue lift was paired with 12% lower 30-day retention and failed the sustainable-growth criterion.

final2.rationale: Maintain the shortened-onboarding experiment. The deeper competitor cut raises the urgency of a response, but the only verified pricing evidence shows a 40% discount reduced 30-day retention by 12% and explicitly failed as a sustainable-growth strategy. Shortened onboarding directly addresses the current completion decline and has verified improvements in completion, time-to-value, and retention; it is the stronger long-term qualified-revenue response under the available evidence. The competitive price pressure remains a material unresolved risk to monitor outside this experiment.
